Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Samir Kaur (Redwood Product Sec), Jared Kim (Orion Head InfoSec), Priya Desai (Orion Compliance), Alan Rivera (Orion Platform), Mei Chen (Orion AppSec)
Links shared: Pen test report: https://redwood.app/attachments/pt-orion-q4-2024.pdf (annotated), SDL C checklist: https://redwood.app/sec/sdlc-checklist, Vulnerability spreadsheet (view-only): https://redwood.app/sheets/orion-vuln

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Quick technical review of pen test results from Q4 2024, discuss vulnerability management flow, patching cadence (monthly vs emergency), secure SDLC gates, and audit log retention. Clarified responsibilities for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) vs hosted and discussed KMS/HSM options.

Topics: pen test findings, CVSS scoring, responsible disclosure / bug bounty, patch cadence, secure SDLC, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, SOC2/ISO evidence mapping, HSM/KMS, private deployment patching responsibilities.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:08] Jared: Jared here from Orion.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, compliance.
[00:12] Alan: Alan, platform eng.
[00:14] Ethan: Ethan Liu, solutions engineer at Redwood.
[00:16] Samir: Samir Kaur, product security.
[00:18] Mei: Mei, app sec.
[00:21] Maya: cool, agenda — go over the pen test highlights, the triage, patching cadence, and then sdlc questions and who's owning what.
[00:30] Jared: perfect. we've already skimmed the executive summary but we'd like the details: in particular the medium finding around some outdated components, and how that maps to your managed vs private deployments.
[00:44] Ethan: yeah, thanks. just to be clear — pen test was done in dec q4 2024 by RedFence (third party), full report attached in the shared link. there were 18 findings; most are low, 3 medium, 0 critical. the medium ones are: CVE-2024-1897 (nginx related misconfig), chain of dependency issue CVE-2024-3344 (python package), and one auth misconfig flagged as potential RBAC bypass in a test harness.
[01:12] Mei: that rbab bypass - can you repeat the scenario? i remember it was hitting an internal admin endpoint via a debug flag?
[01:20] Ethan: um yes, the tester used a staging-only endpoint that had an old debug flag enabled; it allowed escalation to an internal admin call in the harness. important note — this was in an older staging image not shipped to prod for hosted customers, but it is relevant for dedicated / private images where customers opt into allow-debug for troubleshooting.
[01:37] Alan: can we get exact image tags? we run dedicated in our VPC for now so that matters.
[01:42] Ethan: absolute — action item there. I'll add the image tags and the container digests to the triage sheet.
[01:48] Priya: from a compliance pov we need timelines. what's your patch cadence and emergency patch process? monthly? weekly?
[01:55] Samir: our standard policy is monthly security patch cycle for managed/hosted. we do out-of-band emergency patches for P0/P1 vulns which have a CVSS threshold >= 9 or actively exploited. emergency patches have an SLA to customers depending on deployment: hosted we can patch in 24-72 hours, dedicated we notify and coordinate but we can push a hotfix image within 48 hours if the customer allows rolling restarts; private/on-prem obviously depends on customer's ops but we provide the patch and a runbook.
[02:21] Jared: so for our dedicated cluster on aws, you would coordinate the push and we would handle orchestration?
[02:26] Ethan: correct; for Dedicated we provide signed container images and a migration plan. for private on-prem we provide artifacts and step-by-step playbook; we also support KMS envelope keys so that secrets aren't shipped in plaintext.
[02:36] Mei: were any of the reported findings in the core runtime (inference engine) or mostly in infra deps?
[02:42] Samir: mostly infra deps and config mistakes. one medium was a dependency in our auxiliary metrics exporter that had a known cve. the inference kernel paths were audited — no executable-level vulns found in that test.
[02:54] Priya: do you have a bug bounty or responsible disclosure process?
[02:58] Maya: yes we have a responsible disclosure policy and a HackerOne program for some areas; open invite for critical infra issues is handled through private disclosure. the triage sheet shows which reports came from the pen test vs external researchers.
[03:12] Jared: can you confirm retention of audit logs? what are default retention windows and can we increase? we need 7 years for some records.
[03:20] Ethan: default for hosted is 90 days in the UI, 365 days in cold storage optional add-on; for Dedicated we provide an option to ship logs to your SIEM (splunk/datadog/elastic) and retention is customer-managed. we can configure longer retention if you need 7 years, but there are cost & storage considerations — we can export to your S3 with lifecycle policies.
[03:42] Alan: perfect, we will likely ingest into Splunk. what format do you ship logs in?
[03:46] Ethan: JSON lines, with structured fields for token usage, route, model name, request_id, and a hash for PII redaction markers. we also include a request-level trace id for end-to-end correlation.
[03:56] Mei: quick q on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? HSM?
[03:59] Samir: yes. hosted customers can opt into CMK via cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure KeyVault). we also support HSM-backed KMS for Dedicated or Private via an HSM integration (BYO-HSM) and envelope encryption. key rotation policy is 90 days recommended but can be configured.
[04:19] Priya: SOC2 and ISO evidence — can you map the controls and give us the specific artifact locations?
[04:24] Maya: we'll share a SOC2 control matrix that maps to our evidence bundle; Ethan will include links to the screenshots and logs.
[04:29] Ethan: yes i'll upload the mapping doc and sample artifacts — access-controlled links.
[04:32] Jared: back to pen test — are fixes already merged for the medium findings?
[04:36] Samir: we've patched the nginx misconfig (CVE-2024-1897) in hosted images last month; dedicated images are in a staged rollout and we've posted a hotfix image on the registry tagged "patch-2025-02-05". python dep is in progress, PR open to update to the patched version, ETA for deploy is 2025-02-19.
[04:57] Alan: will you provide a benign rollback plan in case of regression? our ops require a tested rollback.
[05:02] Ethan: yes, every release includes a rollback manifest and preflight checks; we'll attach the runbook to the triage sheet.
[05:08] Mei: the report referenced CVSS and some scores were 7.5 — can you share the risk acceptance criteria?
[05:14] Samir: our default is: CVSS >= 9 is P1 (urgent), 7-9 is P2 (medium) with 30 day remediation target, 4-7 is P3 (low) with 90 day target, below that is observation. exceptions can be made with risk acceptance docs.
[05:31] Priya: do you maintain an SBOM? we need component lists for regs.
[05:35] Ethan: yes we generate SBOMs (CycloneDX format) for each image and attach them to releases.
[05:40] Jared: great. question on secure SDLC — how are security gates enforced? are there automated SAST/DAST hooks in CI?
[05:47] Samir: we run SAST on PRs, dependency scanning (OSS vuln scanning) and DAST nightly against staging. PRs blocking on security findings for sensitive modules are required to have a mitigation or ticket before merge. we also log all findings in Jira and have a 3-day SLA to triage new findings.
[06:06] Mei: for third-party libs, what's cadence for dependency updates?
[06:10] Samir: we do weekly dependency monitoring; critical updates are fast-tracked. we also have scheduled quarterly dependency refreshes for non-critical packages.
[06:20] Alan: patching cadence for OS and host kernels? we manage the container images and base images monthly; for host-level kernel patches on dedicated we provide guidance and optional managed host updates through our ops team if contracted.
[06:34] Jared: any residual risks we should be aware of?
[06:36] Ethan: the main residual is customer-enabled debug flags in dedicated/private images; recommended mitigation is to disable debug by default and require an explicit opt-in with an ACL tied to RBAC.
[06:46] Priya: about RBAC — does Redwood integrate with our SSO (Okta SAML) and can we map roles to least privilege?
[06:51] Maya: yes SAML/Okta supported; you can map groups to Redwood roles. we also support SCIM for provisioning.
[06:58] Mei: are admin-level audit trails immutable? we need tamper-evident logs.
[07:02] Samir: we support append-only logs shipped to customer-owned S3 buckets with object-lock if required, and we can integrate with your WORM policies; we also sign activity logs with a runtime signature so any tampering is detectable.
[07:16] Jared: ok good. one more — will you run a remediation verification scan post fixes?
[07:20] Ethan: yes we offer a re-test option; we can either re-run automated scans or coordinate with RedFence for a re-test (paid). we'll include a re-test plan in the follow-up.
[07:29] Priya: timeline wise — we need documented evidence for SOC2 audit in march — can you commit to providing the artifacts by feb 20?
[07:36] Maya: we'll do our best; Ethan and I will prioritize the SOC2 evidence packet and the pen test annotated triage.
[07:41] Alan: note — we'll apply the nginx patch in our staging cluster by monday and share results.
[07:46] Ethan: thanks, please tag us on the ticket.
[07:49] Maya: okay quick recap and next steps — ethan will share the triage, i (maya) will send the SOC2 mapping, alan will confirm patch in staging, jared/priya will confirm retention numbers — we set a follow-up two weeks out.
[07:59] Jared: sounds good.
[08:01] Mei: thanks everyone.
[08:05] Maya: end.
